title: What If You Never Wrote by Hand Again?

scenes.text: What if you never wrote by hand again? Your keyboard would win the race and lose the test.
Typing is fast. Students on laptops take down far more words in a lecture.
But in a Princeton study, they did worse on the conceptual questions afterwards.
Laptop note-takers copied lectures word for word instead of putting ideas in their own words.
In 2024, Norwegian scientists put 256 sensors on students' heads. Handwriting lit up brain networks that typing didn't.
Slow is the point. The effort of shaping every letter may be what makes it stick.

description:
In a 2014 Psychological Science study (Princeton and UCLA), students who took lecture notes on laptops wrote more words but more verbatim, and did worse on conceptual questions than students writing by hand.
In a 2024 study at the Norwegian University of Science and Technology, 256-electrode EEG showed far more widespread brain connectivity when students wrote by hand than when they typed. Later replication attempts of the note-taking result have been mixed.
